cards.explanation: The answer is that they did evil in His sight. Judges 6:1 says, “Again the Israelites did evil in the sight of the LORD…” Look at that word “Again.” This wasn't their first time down this road. So He delivered them into the hand of Midian for seven years, and that's a long stretch, friends.

The answer is up in the mountains and caves. Judges 6:2 says they prepared shelters “…in the mountains, caves, and strongholds.” That's where the Israelites set up because of the Midianites. I've slept in a junk drawer, so I know a rough bed when I hear one, and caves don't sound like a step up.
The word is “destroy.” Judges 6:4 says they were “…destroying the produce of the land.” Verse 3 says this happened whenever the Israelites planted their crops. Plant a crop, and here they come.

The answer is a great swarm of locusts. Judges 6:5 says they came “…like a great swarm of locusts.” Think of a cloud of hungry bugs landing on a field, except this cloud has tents and camels. That's the picture the Bible paints.

The answer is False. They could not be counted. Judges 6:5 says, “They and their camels were innumerable…” and they “…entered the land to ravage it.” Imagine trying to count that crowd. You'd lose your place before you got started.

The word is “prophet.” Judges 6:8 says, “He sent them a prophet…” A prophet is someone who speaks for God, so this man comes carrying the LORD's own message. Israel cried out, and the LORD answered with words for them.

The answer is not to fear the gods of the Amorites. The LORD says, “I am the LORD your God. You must not fear the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you dwell.” (Judges 6:10). The Amorites were people who lived in the land. It's a plain reminder of who Israel's God is.

The answer is False. The LORD does not say Israel obeyed Him. The message ends with Him saying, “But you did not obey Me.” (Judges 6:10). It follows a list of what He had done for them. Hard words, but the prophet says them straight.

The answer is in a winepress. Judges 6:11 says Gideon, Joash's son, was “…threshing wheat in a winepress to hide it from the Midianites.” I think a winepress is a strange place to thresh wheat, but I'd guess that's the idea. You hide your wheat where nobody's looking.

The answer is “mighty man of valor.” The angel says, “The LORD is with you, O mighty man of valor.” (Judges 6:12). And remember where Gideon is standing when he hears it: in a winepress, hiding wheat. That's quite a greeting for that spot.

The answer is “Then why has all this happened to us.” Gideon says, “if the LORD is with us, why has all this happened to us?” (Judges 6:13). He doesn't tiptoe around it. He opens with “Please, my Lord…” and then he asks the hard question out loud.

The answer is True. Gideon says, “But now the LORD has forsaken us and delivered us into the hand of Midian.” (Judges 6:13). Those are his words, said out loud to the angel. He holds nothing back, friends.

The job is to save Israel from Midian. The LORD says, “Go in the strength you have and save Israel from the hand of Midian.” (Judges 6:14). That job lands on the man who was threshing wheat in a winepress to hide it from the Midianites (Judges 6:11). I bet Gideon did not see that coming.

The word is “weakest.” Gideon says, “…my clan is the weakest in Manasseh…” (Judges 6:15). Manasseh was one of Israel's tribes. He lists his weak spots like he's reading a résumé nobody should hire. And I'm in no position to laugh, since I started out in a 25 cent bin.

The answer is False. Gideon says he is the youngest, not the oldest. His words are, “…I am the youngest in my father’s house.” (Judges 6:15). He says it right after calling his clan the weakest in Manasseh. He's stacking up his reasons like dough bowls.

The word is “sign.” Gideon says, “…give me a sign that it is You speaking with me.” (Judges 6:17). Then he asks the LORD to wait while he brings an offering, and the LORD says, “I will stay until you return.” (Judges 6:18).

The answer is a young goat and unleavened bread. Judges 6:19 says Gideon “…prepared a young goat and unleavened bread and an ephah of flour.” He put the meat in a basket and the broth in a pot. That's real cooking, friends, and I respect the work.

The answer is that fire flares up from the rock. Judges 6:21 says, “…fire flared from the rock and consumed the meat and the unleavened bread.” The angel only touched them with the tip of his staff. Fire out of a rock from one touch of a staff is quite a thing to watch.
The answer is False. After the fire, “…the angel of the LORD vanished from his sight.” (Judges 6:21). He was there one moment and gone the next. That's when Gideon realizes who he's been talking to.

The answer is that he saw the angel face to face. Gideon says, “Oh no, Lord GOD! I have seen the angel of the LORD face to face!” (Judges 6:22). That's what he says happened. I think that's a man who just got a big surprise.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “Peace be with you. Do not be afraid, for you will not die.” (Judges 6:23). Gideon had just cried out in alarm, and these are the words that answer him. Short, calm and clear.

The answer is “The LORD Is Peace.” Gideon “…called it The LORD Is Peace.” (Judges 6:24). It comes right after the LORD told him, “Peace be with you.” And the text says the altar still stood in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.

The answer is his father's altar to Baal. The LORD says, “…tear down your father’s altar to Baal…” (Judges 6:25). Baal is a false god, and this altar belongs to Gideon's father. So the job hits Gideon's own family first.

The answer is a proper altar to the LORD. The LORD says, “…build a proper altar to the LORD your God on the top of this stronghold.” (Judges 6:26). Out goes the altar to Baal, and up goes an altar to the LORD. The wood of the Asherah pole is used for the burnt offering.

The answer is False. They did not do it in broad daylight. Judges 6:27 says he “…did it by night rather than in the daytime.” He took ten of his servants along. With a whole altar to tear down, that's a big night's work.

The answer is that he fears his father's household and the city. Judges 6:27 says he was “…too afraid of his father’s household and the men of the city…” so he did it by night. The text gives us that reason plainly. He still did what the LORD told him, afraid and all.

The answer is True. Judges 6:28 says, “…there was Baal’s altar torn down, with the Asherah pole cut down beside it and the second bull offered up on the newly built altar.” Imagine waking up to that view. It's all sitting there for them to see.

The word is “die.” The men of the city say, “Bring out your son. He must die…” (Judges 6:30). They give a reason too: he tore down Baal's altar and cut down the Asherah pole. This is a heavy moment for Gideon, and I think it's good to say so plainly.

The answer is False. Joash does not hand Gideon over. The men tell him, “Bring out your son.” and he says to all who stood against him, “If Baal is a god, let him contend for himself with the one who has torn down his altar.” (Judges 6:31). The text shows him answering them with a challenge. It doesn't show him handing Gideon over.

The answer is that Baal should contend for himself. Joash says, “If Baal is a god, let him contend for himself with the one who has torn down his altar.” (Judges 6:31). Baal's the one with the broken altar, so let him do the talking. It's a sharp answer from a man with a whole crowd in front of him.

The answer is “Let Baal contend with him.” That's what Jerubbaal means, and Judges 6:32 says Gideon got the name because he had torn down Baal’s altar. The man who was hiding wheat now has a brand new name. And it picks up Joash's own challenge.
